sentences: `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32` is now **exact round-toward-zero** (finite overflow gives ±65504, not inf).
The GPU smoke test caught the old round-to-nearest version producing inf in `PS_ImposterShadow`.

The other f16 packs (`v_cvt_f16_f32`, d16 results, mix ops) round to nearest, which matches the default mode; the ALU ones follow a MODE toward-zero write (below; `v_fma_mixlo/mixhi_f16` round the exact `x*y+z` once in every mode (measured on an RDNA2 iGPU, gfx1036, 7 of 7 discriminating tie inputs, SHADER-135); the translator does that in both modes through `Gen.fma_mix_odd`; the ALU ones follow a MODE toward-zero write (below; `v_fma_mixlo/mixhi_f16` round the exact `x*y+z` once in every mode (measured on an RDNA2 iGPU, gfx1036, 7 of 7 discriminating tie inputs, SHADER-135); toward zero the translator does that already, while in nearest-even mode it still narrows an f32 `Fma`, which is 1 f16 ulp off on ties until #1774 (SHADER-296) lands; the ALU ones follow a MODE toward-zero write (below; ALU sites: see the f16 rounding row).

MODE: `s_setreg_imm32_b32 hwreg(HW_REG_MODE, 2, 2)` (f16/f64 rounding) is tracked in a per-invocation variable, the only MODE field the corpus writes (9,417 writes in 6,333 shaders: 6,694 toward zero, 2,723 back to nearest even).

While it is toward zero, every VALU f16 result except the transcendentals listed below (`v_cvt_f16_f32`, f16 arithmetic, `v_pk_*_f16`, `v_fma_mix{lo,hi}_f16`, `v_interp_p2_f16`) rounds toward zero exactly, with the integer conversion `v_cvt_pkrtz_f16_f32` uses (`f16_bits(rtz=True)`, see the f16 rounding row), and `v_add_f64` steps back one ulp when the TwoSum error shows it rounded away from zero; finite overflow gives the largest finite value.
The `v_add_f64` output modifiers apply after that step and round to nearest, so an omod that overflows or lands on a subnormal is not toward zero.

**omod versus denormal mode is unmodelled:** the translator applies `mul:2`/`mul:4`/`div:2` regardless of the MODE denormal fields (as before this change), whereas hardware ignores omod when denormals are kept (denorm fields = 3) and applies it when they are flushed (both measured on an RX 6800: `v_add_f64 (1 - 2^-60) mul:2` with denormals kept gave 3ff00000:00000000 nearest and 3fefffff:ffffffff toward zero, unscaled; mul:2 was applied with denormals flushed); the tests therefore claim no omod order.

CPU-checked by `tests/test_mode_round.py` (the RX 6800 words for f16 add/sub, `v_fma_mix`, the transcendentals, f64 overflow). f16 add and sub (f16 operands) and `v_pk_add_f16` take the exact TwoSum error of the f32 result into account, so they are exact toward zero too (f32 then f16 rounding alone would be wrong: 2 - 2^-24 is an f32 tie that rounds up to 2.0); f16 FMAs need nothing extra, since their round-to-odd f32 value (SHADER-55) narrows exactly in either mode.

`v_fma_mix{lo,hi}_f16` rounds the exact fma once, straight to f16, in both nearest-even and toward-zero modes (measured on AMD RDNA2 gfx1036, finding 7079901079; an RX 6800 gave 0x3fff for 1 * 2 - 2^-30, where rounding to f32 first and then narrowing gives 0x4000): `v_fma_mix{lo,hi}_f16` rounds the exact fma once, straight to f16, in both nearest-even and toward-zero modes (measured on AMD RDNA2 gfx1036 across 7 of 7 discriminating tie inputs with `tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw`, SHADER-135, finding 7079901079, and on an RX 6800 where toward zero gave 0x3fff for 1 * 2 - 2^-30 vs 0x4000 with double rounding; fixed for nearest mode in SHADER-296 / #1774; see docs/shader_validation.md, "`v_fma_mix*` f16 rounding in nearest mode"): `v_fma_mix{lo,hi}_f16` rounds the exact fma once, straight to f16, toward zero (an RX 6800 gave 0x3fff for 1 * 2 - 2^-30, where rounding to f32 first and then narrowing gives 0x4000): `v_fma_mix{lo,hi}_f16` rounds the exact fma once, straight to f16, in both nearest-even and toward-zero modes (measured on AMD RDNA2 gfx1036 and verified by `tools/fma_mix_probe.py`; finding 7079901079; toward zero an RX 6800 gave 0x3fff for 1 * 2 - 2^-30, where rounding to f32 first and then narrowing gives 0x4000): `Gen.fma_mix_odd` corrects the f32 `Fma` to round-to-odd by the sign of its exact residual (product error by `Fma(x, y, -x*y)`, TwoSum of the sum), which narrows exactly in either direction; the nearest-even path is unchanged (f32 `Fma`, then narrow).

`fma_mix_odd` also handles a tiny product ( | a x*y | >= < 2^-64: its error underflows or is flushed, so the residual sign is sign(x) xor sign(y), independent of the driver's denormal mode) and an f32 overflow with finite operands (toward zero gives ±FLT_MAX, so f16 ±65504).

`v_rcp_f16`, `v_rsq_f16`, `v_sqrt_f16`, `v_sin_f16`, `v_cos_f16`, `v_exp_f16` and `v_log_f16` ignore the rounding mode on hardware, so they always narrow to nearest even; all seven are measured (an RX 6700 XT gave the same words with FP_ROUND round-toward-zero and round-to-nearest on every input of each; see the f16 transcendentals row).

`v_rcp_f16`, `v_rsq_f16`, `v_sqrt_f16`, `v_sin_f16`, `v_cos_f16`, `v_exp_f16` and `v_log_f16` ignore the rounding mode on hardware (RX 6800 for the first four, plus an exhaustive 65,536-input RNE vs RTZ sweep of all seven in wave32 and wave64 on native `gfx1036` via `tools/mode_round_probe.py`, SHADER-132: 0/65,536 inputs differ on every op; the same probe also confirmed all 17 f16/f64 RNE vs RTZ cases including `v_cvt_f16_f32`, `v_add/sub/mul/fma_f16`, `v_pk_add/fma_f16`, `v_fma_mix{lo,hi}_f16` and `v_add_f64` overflow saturation in both wave32 and wave64), so they always narrow to nearest even.

In nearest mode the hardware rounds once as well: `v_rcp_f16`, `v_rsq_f16`, `v_sqrt_f16`, `v_sin_f16`, `v_cos_f16`, `v_exp_f16` and `v_log_f16` ignore the rounding mode on hardware, so they always narrow to nearest even; all seven are measured (an RX 6700 XT gave the same words with FP_ROUND round-toward-zero and round-to-nearest on every input of each, see the f16 transcendentals row; independently confirmed by an exhaustive 65,536-input RNE vs RTZ sweep of all seven in wave32 and wave64 on native `gfx1036` via `tools/mode_round_probe.py`, SHADER-132: `v_rcp_f16`, `v_rsq_f16`, `v_sqrt_f16` and `v_sin_f16` ignore the rounding mode on hardware (RX 6800: the same words in every mode), so they always narrow to nearest even; `v_cos_f16`, `v_exp_f16` and `v_log_f16` are unmeasured, assumed like those four and treated the same.
The "every VALU f16 result rounds toward zero" sentence above therefore excludes these seven; the f16 results of `v_floor/ceil/trunc/rndne/fract_f16` are exact and need no rounding.

`tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw` on an RDNA2 iGPU (gfx1036, SHADER-135) gave the single-rounded word for all seven inputs where the two rules differ by one f16 ulp, as `Gen.fma_mix_odd` produces (docs/shader_validation.md, "`v_fma_mix*` f16 rounding in nearest mode").

In nearest mode the translator still rounds `v_fma_mix{lo,hi}_f16` twice (f32 `Fma`, then narrow), but the hardware rounds once there as well: `tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw` on an RDNA2 iGPU (gfx1036, SHADER-135) gave the single-rounded word for all seven inputs where the two rules differ by one f16 ulp, so the translator, which rounded twice there (f32 `Fma`, then narrow) until #1774, was one f16 ulp off on exactly those ties (docs/shader_validation.md, "`v_fma_mix*` f16 rounding in nearest mode"; the fix is `Gen.fma_mix_odd` in nearest mode too, SHADER-296).
Nearest-mode `v_fma_mix*` still rounds twice (f32 `Fma`, then narrow): main's behaviour, unmeasured.
`tools/fma_mix_probe.py --oracle hw` measures it on an AMD GPU, with seven inputs where the two rules differ by one f16 ulp (docs/shader_validation.md).
The `v_add_f64` step needs f64 denormals preserved (not flushed) by the driver for subnormal sums.
Shaders that never write MODE emit the same code as without this.
Writes to other MODE bits (f32 rounding, denormals), directed rounding (+inf/-inf) and register-valued writes are refused, so nothing changes silently; none occur in the corpus.
Denormal behaviour is still Vulkan's default.
Format conversions in memory and texture units don't follow MODE.
